From: Alex Grant <alex@edenbridge.ai>

Cc: procurement@edenbridge.ai

Subject: Dedicated sizing for real-time assistant (tokens/sec ask)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team loved the latency and predictability. We got internal buy-in to run a pilot and need a recommended Dedicated capacity profile so we can scope procurement. Quick background:
- Workload: customer-facing assistant for account support, avg prompt+response ~1.2k tokens, bursts to 12k tokens in multi-step sessions.
- Target SLO: 95th percentile p95 response under 400ms for single-turn chat (we know this is tight).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~45 requests/sec initially, grows to 180 rps over 6 months.
- Typical model candidate: open-llm-7b, quantized to 4-bit; we may evaluate a 13B variant if quality demands.

Can you send a tokens-per-second estimate mapped to GPU SKU recommendations and a conservative headroom buffer for peaking (we want an ops-safe slab allocation + a burst policy)? Procurement will need an order of magnitude cost estimate too.

Appreciate a short runbook or spreadsheet we can attach to the SOW.

- Alex
Head of Product, EdenBridge

[Attachment: edenbridge_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Alex Grant <alex@edenbridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for real-time assistant (tokens/sec ask)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Ben (capacity) and Karthik (solutions) for ops + workload assumptions. I sketched a first-pass model and attached a worksheet with the math and two SKU options. High level summary below, followed by assumptions and next steps.

High-level recommendation (pilot -> initial commit):
- Model: open-llm-7b quant4 (recommended), fallback option: open-13b-qat for quality testing.
- Steady-state mapping: 45 rps -> ~9k tokens/sec aggregate (assuming 1.2k avg tokens * 45 rps -> 54k tokens/sec generated? see assumptions)
- We present two sizing strategies:
  1) Conservative slab (latency-first): 6 A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (continuous) + 2 spare for burst = supports p95 < 350–400ms for 7b quant under current prompt distribution.
  2) Cost-balanced slab: 4 A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs + autoscale burst pool (2 GPUs) with prefix/KV warm cache tuning — keeps cost lower but requires careful warmup policy.
- Headroom: recommend 40–60% headroom above observed steady-state tokens/sec for first 90 days, then re-evaluate after traffic telemetry.

Key tokens/sec math (summary):
- Client RTT/overhead excluded; modeling focuses on server-side token throughput.
- Average tokens per request (T): 1,200 tokens round-trip.
- Req/sec (R): 45 -> tokens/sec demand D = T * R = 54,000 tokens/sec (aggregate consumption).
- Effective tokens/sec per A100-equivalent for open-llm-7b (quant4) with batching and KV cache: ~10k–12k tokens/sec (p95 latency budget) depending on batch.
- So 54k / 11k ≈ 4.9 -> round up to 6 GPUs for latency-first buffer.

Assumptions and caveats:
- We assumed continuity of KV cache effectiveness; if sessions are highly unique (low reuse) effective per-GPU TPS drops ~20–30%.
- 95th latency depends heavily on batch sizing and tail contention — we included continuous batching and a small hot-prefix cache in the workbook.
- If you evaluate 13B for quality, expect per-GPU tokens/sec to drop ~45–55%; plan for ~2x GPUs for parity.

Attachments: edenbridge_compute_model_v1.xlsx (workbook with scenario tabs), rbw-tiling-slab-summary.pdf (one-pager).

Next steps:
1) Ben + Karthik to validate slab counts and confirm A100-equivalent SKU choices.
2) We'll add a burst policy clause (on-demand GPUs up to X) and draft cost ranges for procurement.
3) Provision a short telemetry plan (prompts, token histograms, p95 latency checks) for first 30 days.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: EdenBridge - tiling & peaking capacity play

Adding a few ops-focused notes from capacity planning side:

Operational tiling & peaking proposal (practical runbook):
- Tiling strategy: group persistent sessions on a warm slab (pin hot prefixes). Reserve one GPU per 20–25 sustained rps of the model variant. For your 45 rps baseline that matches 2–3 GPUs pinned, remaining throughput via balanced slab.
- Burst policy: provision 2 hot-warm GPUs in the same AZ for <3 minute bursts. Use immediate fallback to a 13B-quant degraded model only if quality must trade for capacity.
- Pre-warm cache: recommend seeding cache during business hours (00:00–01:00 UTC) and a TTL of 12 hours for session keys.
- Safety buffers: maintain a 15% operational reserve in Dedicated fleet for maintenance rotations.

Concrete SKU mapping (example):
- A100-80GB equivalent (prod): 1 GPU ≈ 11k tokens/sec (7b quant).
- V100-equivalent (older): ~6k tokens/sec (avoid for latency-tight SLOs).

Cost ballpark (monthly, USD):
- Conservative slab (6 prod GPUs + 2 burst): ~$120k–140k/month (incl infra, reserved commit discounts applied).
- Cost-balanced (4 prod + 2 burst): ~$85k–95k/month but expect higher p95 variance during peaking.

Operational asks for EdenBridge procurement:
- Contract should include a short-term burst allowance (on-demand) and an SLA for burst provisioning within <3 minutes for AZ-local resources.
- We'll provide an ops playbook and SLO dashboard pre-configured in Redwood Console as part of Dedicated onboarding.

I attached a one-page slab-summary for non-technical procurement folks. Happy to run this by your finance team.

—Ben
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: rbw-tiling-slab-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

Jasmine / Ben — this is perfect, thank you. Procurement reviewed the conservative slab and prefers to start with the cost-balanced option with a documented burst SLA (we want to avoid over-committing on month 1). A few quick asks before we sign: 

1) Can you add an explicit example of the burst activation flow (who calls API, expected time-to-warm, fallback behavior)?
2) Please include an entry in the workbook that shows a 13B variant swap scenario with explicit GPU counts and monthly delta.
3) Can we get the first 30-day telemetry event list (metrics + alert thresholds) you mentioned? Procurement wants this as an appendix to the SOW.

If you can get these to me by EOD Tuesday we can route the SOW to legal and get a PO started.

Thanks again — Alex
Head of Product, EdenBridge
